principles: List construction must be proportional to the visible window, not the backing collection — where the component windows at all. Where it does not, say so and budget the host instead.
A scroll container bounds its own height. One that does not cannot scroll, and a virtual window measured from clientHeight then covers the whole list.
Stable item identity is required for scroll restoration and focused-row continuity.
Media decoding, upload progress, and message updates must be scoped to the affected item.

message10k.budget: Host keeps a bounded projection; the component renders it in full (see measuredBudgets.messageList)

message100kEstimated.budget: Host retains a bounded projection and stable reading anchor

manyImages.budget: Decode near viewport; thumbnail before original

uploadQueue.budget: Progress update rebuilds only the changed transfer row

measuredBudgets.note: Measured by website/tests/performance-budget.spec.ts against /resources/performance-regression at 1440x900. Ceilings sit above the observed numbers with room for machine noise; they exist to catch a regression in kind (windowing switched off, a row's node count doubling), not to police milliseconds. Observed values are from a 2026-09-15 run on the dev server (mount was 1153 ms on 2026-09-13 and 7.2 s before the Round 5 fix, when every message built its own menu popover); re-record them when the numbers move.

conversationList.why: FlareConversationList windows above 200 items. 1000 items render a screenful plus overscan.

messageList.why: FlareMessageList keeps loaded timelines on native layout on purpose: its row heights vary with rich text, media and quotes, and a fixed-estimate window makes the scrollbar jump under paging. The DOM is therefore O(loaded), and the bound belongs to the host's paging window — not to a claim the component does not keep.

mount.why: Both lists mounted with the full load on a dev server. A ceiling this loose still catches an order-of-magnitude regression.
